scopes.headline: Error and danger states have no semantic role. They paint the mode-invariant --a63-action-danger fill, which measures 2.98:1 on the dark page, and Alert ships it. The Tailwind bridge offers no text-danger, text-accent or text-tertiary, so consumers reach for text-destructive and text-primary, which the new role check flags.

The contract layer is not a complete or enforced source of truth. Only 3 of 76 contracts declare intent, and only 2 of the 31 cross-renderer contracts map their axes to iOS. Maturity is self-declared, so 69 contracts say stable, and one exported component (progressive-blur) has no contract at all but still shows as Stable.

The biggest problem is that AppView is the only frame that owns safe-area insets. AppShell, which runs four app pages, and the full-page chat own none, even though the starter ships viewport-fit=cover, so on iPhone their content and the chat composer run under the notch and the home indicator.
最大问题是发布流水线：每次 beta 发布都卡在移动 npm 的 latest 标签这一步（trusted publisher 报 403，没开 "Allow npm dist-tag"），所以 8 个包的 latest 都落后于 beta，发布后的 git tag 和 registry 证据也一直没记录下来，README 说的「直接 npm install 就能装到 beta」现在不成立。

The agent-facing docs are wrong where agents read them: mdx-to-markdown.ts strips import, export and JSX lines even inside code fences, so `atom63 docs` and the published .md twins serve empty or headless code samples on 16 of 31 pages. On top of that, the iOS API (68 of 101 types) and several web entry points are not in the agent index at all.

The default Toggle's pressed state cannot be seen: in the default modern theme (and in aqua) a pressed neutral Toggle measures 1.00:1 against an unpressed one, with the same text colour. Its baselines recorded this without anything failing.

None of the 8 choice-and-range components is ready, though all are marked stable: state is drawn only with background-color or color and has no forced-colors fallback (radio, progress, rating), RTL is broken (the switch thumb leaves its track, and the slider gets no DirectionProvider), and the SegmentedControl and ranged Slider APIs cannot be named or controlled.

The form layer cannot show or announce errors end to end: Field never links its description or error to the control, and Select and Autocomplete have no invalid state at all, so an invalid form looks valid wherever a select or autocomplete is used.

The biggest problem is that the overlays' open state is almost never captured: every Dialog, AlertDialog, Sheet and HoverCard baseline shows only the closed trigger, and so do the default Toaster and the iOS sheet, alert and toast snapshots. The surfaces themselves are unguarded, axe never audits them, and nobody can judge them in the 4 x 2 themes.

Keyboard focus and selection in this batch exist only as background fills with outline:none, and no forced-colors rule exists outside button.css. In Windows High Contrast the focused row of every menu (DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, Menubar, Command) and the selected tab both disappear.

The biggest problem: none of the 10 batch-6 surfaces is ready, yet every contract says stable. The one blocker is ScrollableList: its chevron buttons unmount while they have focus, so keyboard focus drops to the body. Behind that are repeated gaps. No forced-colors handling, so separator and resizable lines vanish. Disabled, hover and focus states are never captured. No RTL, CJK or phone-width stories.

The biggest problem: the app-frame navigation is not reliably usable without sight. A collapsed offcanvas Sidebar stays in the tab order while it is off-screen, and no active Sidebar or Nav Tree item ever sets aria-current. So keyboard users land on links they cannot see, and screen-reader users cannot tell which page they are on.

The biggest problem: in any dark-scoped UIProvider the Skeleton is drawn light grey (240,240,240 on a 25,25,25 panel) in all four themes, because --a63-skeleton-base is only declared on :root. The broken render is committed as the visual baseline.

Both screen-reader promises in this batch are probably broken: VoiceOver likely drops the message text on iOS (the explicit label replaces the combined one), and the typing indicator likely announces nothing because it is named only by aria-label and always sits inside an aria-busy ChatMessage.

On iOS, action fill tokens (actionDanger, actionPrimary, the same value in both modes) are used as text and icon colors with no Swift role check and no textDanger counterpart, which causes the dark-mode contrast failures (2.5-3:1) in AtomNotice, AtomContentStateView and the selection and dot indicators; no subject is ready, because the iOS snapshots also cover only the standard theme.

InformSpotlight is a blocking modal (scrim, scroll lock, inert page, focus trap) whose only exits are Escape or an action, with no dismiss button and no scrim click, so on a phone, or for anyone with no Escape key, a spotlight without actions cannot be closed.

findings.subject: progressive-blur
findings.summary: ProgressiveBlur is an exported, documented component with no contract at all, so its axes (ProgressiveBlurPosition), defaults, slots and states are nowhere in the contract layer.
findings.evidence: No packages/ui-foundation/contracts/components/progressive-blur.json; packages/ui-react/src/components/progressive-blur/{progressive-blur.tsx,stories,test} exist; `pnpm -s atom63 component progressive-blur` prints "Status: Stable" and "TypeScript remains the source of truth for complete prop contracts" with no axes; agent-index.json entry has `contract: null`.
findings.fix: Write contracts/components/progressive-blur.json (positions axis, default, slots, states, maturity preview until scored), run generate:contracts and generate:index.

verified.reason: Reproduced. There is no contracts/components/progressive-blur.json, while ui-react/src/components/progressive-blur/{tsx,stories,test} exist. In agent-index.json it is the only one of 76 entries with `contract: null` and `axisGuidance: null`, and it exports ProgressiveBlurPosition. A missing contract meets P0 = missing. No documented exemption found; production-readiness-audit.md:78 only notes its missing recipe.

findings.subject: toggle
findings.summary: A pressed Toggle with the default neutral tone looks exactly like an unpressed one in modern light, aqua light and aqua dark (fill contrast 1.00:1, same text colour), and below 1.25:1 in every other theme.
findings.evidence: Pixel measurement of apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-toggle-themes-chromium-linux.png (points 124,y vs 260,y) and ui-react-toggle-states-chromium-linux.png (1.03:1); packages/ui-react/src/components/toggle/toggle.css:25-31,137-141 fall back to --a63-segment-selected-background (surface-overlay in modern, surface-panel in aqua).
findings.fix: Give standalone Toggle its own pressed fill token (e.g. --a63-selected-background or surface-muted/control-active) that differs from the page by at least 3:1 non-text contrast or add a second cue (weight or border), set per theme; add a check that the pressed and rest baselines differ.

verified.reason: The themes snapshot shows the neutral 'On' toggle with no visible fill and the same text weight and colour as 'Off' in modern/light, aqua/light and aqua/dark. Only modern/dark, retro and terminal show a faint pill. toggle.css:137-141 paints only --toggle-on-background/foreground. Those fall back to --a63-segment-selected-background, which is surface-overlay in modern.css:32 and surface-panel in aqua.css:93, and the foreground is text-primary, the same as at rest. neutral is the contract's defaultTone, so the default pressed state is invisible: P0 under 'wrong'.

findings.subject: @atom63/mdx, @atom63/inform, @atom63/agent, @atom63/widgets
findings.summary: Four published TypeScript packages have no API report and no tier inventory, so their public type changes are invisible in review and nothing says which exports are stable.
findings.evidence: scripts/design-system/api-report.mjs:2-3 claims 'every entry point of the published TypeScript packages' but its map (api-report.mjs:23-33) holds only ui-foundation and ui-react; no packages/{mdx,inform,agent,widgets}/api/ folder exists (find -name '*.api.md' -> ui-react x7, ui-foundation x1). They expose 14, 4, 2 and 5 export keys (docs/design-system/audits/package-surface.json). Tier inventory exists only for ui-react (docs/design-system/audits/ui-react-export-inventory.json).
findings.fix: Add each package's typed entries to the api-report.mjs map (mdx 9 typed entries, inform 3, agent 2, widgets 4), commit the reports, and extend the export-inventory audit (or a per-package tier field) to these packages.

verified.reason: api-report.mjs:2-3 says it covers 'every entry point of the published TypeScript packages', but the map at lines 23-33 holds only ui-foundation and ui-react. The only api folders are ui-foundation, ui-react and ui-ios. published-packages.mjs lists mdx, inform, agent and widgets as published, and none of them has a report. I found no documented exemption.

findings.subject: @atom63/mdx, @atom63/inform, @atom63/agent, @atom63/widgets
findings.summary: Four published packages are never installed by any consumer smoke test, from tarball or from the registry, and the stable preflight covers only 3 of the 8 published packages.
findings.evidence: scripts/design-system/smoke-registry-ui-react.mjs:20-25 requests styles, ui-foundation, ui-react, cli only; pack smoke tarballs are the same four (scratchpad/sweep/ds-pack-smoke.log 'Tarballs: @atom63/styles ..., @atom63/ui-foundation ..., @atom63/ui-react ..., @atom63/cli ...'); scripts/design-system/audit-stable-release-preflight.mjs:10 packageDirs = styles, ui-foundation, ui-react; docs/design-system/audits/stable-release-preflight.json lists 3 packages. publishedPackageDirs (scripts/design-system/published-packages.mjs) lists 8.
findings.fix: Add mdx, inform, agent and widgets to the pack and registry smoke consumers (import one export from every entry and its styles.css, typecheck and vite build), and drive the stable preflight from publishedPackageDirs instead of a hard-coded list of 3.

verified.reason: smoke-registry-ui-react.mjs:20-25 installs only styles, ui-foundation, ui-react and cli. smoke-packed-ui-react.mjs:15-22 covers the same four. audit-stable-release-preflight.mjs:10 packageDirs lists 3 packages, while published-packages.mjs lists 8. These are the only smoke and pack scripts, and no other script installs mdx, inform, agent or widgets as a consumer would.

findings.subject: apps/docs (docs coverage and Markdown twins)
findings.summary: The Markdown twins that agents read (`atom63 docs`, system.atom63.io/*.md) drop code lines inside fenced blocks: 111 lines across 16 of 31 pages, including import lines and whole JSX samples.
findings.evidence: apps/docs/src/lib/mdx-to-markdown.ts:77-100 skips lines starting with import/export/</{/* without tracking ``` fences. `pnpm -s atom63 docs pattern-widgets` lines 70-72 print an empty ```tsx block where pattern-widgets.mdx:155-162 has the WidgetGrid sample; `curl https://system.atom63.io/patterns/pattern-widgets.md` lines 70-71 match. pattern-agent.mdx:146,239,265-267 import lines are gone from the twin; pattern-inform twin starts with stray demo code and loses `export const registry = defineInformRegistry([` (mdx:77). Per-page loss: pattern-widgets 22, pattern-layout 18, pattern-local-layout 14, foundation-effects 9, pattern-inform 8, foundation-surface-model 7. No mdx-to-markdown test exists.
findings.fix: Track fence state in mdxToMarkdown and pass fenced lines through verbatim; strip only top-level MDX imports, exports and JSX. Add apps/docs/src/lib/mdx-to-markdown.test.ts with a fenced import, export and JSX sample; regenerate the agent index.

verified.reason: Reproduced. In apps/docs/src/lib/mdx-to-markdown.ts the loop drops any line whose trimmed text starts with `import`, `export`, `<` or `{/*`, and it never tracks ``` fences. pattern-widgets.mdx:155-162 holds a full WidgetGrid sample (an import line plus JSX). `pnpm -s atom63 docs pattern-widgets` prints that block as an empty ```tsx fence. Only mdx-to-markdown.ts and vite-plugins/llms-txt.ts reference mdxToMarkdown, so no test covers it. The twin is what agents read, and losing the code samples breaks U1 for the docs subject. I did not recount the per-page line totals.

findings.subject: packages/cli (atom63 CLI and MCP)
findings.summary: The iOS API is not findable through the CLI or MCP: 68 of 101 public Atom* Swift types are absent from the agent index, including the ones Round 13a found iOS builders missed.
findings.evidence: grep of `public (struct|enum|class|protocol) Atom*` in packages/ui-ios gives 101 names; 68 appear nowhere in packages/cli/generated/agent-index.json (AtomAppBar, AtomAppBarStyle, AtomDensity, AtomMessageDeliveryState, AtomListRow, AtomIconButton, AtomInformArbiter, ...). `pnpm -s atom63 search AtomAppBar`, `AtomMessage`, `atomDensity` -> 'No results'. case-studies-round-13a.md:41-45: iOS builders 'read the ui-ios README and the MCP' and adoption of compact density and AtomAppBar was 1 of 7 until the README (not the index) was fixed in #283.
findings.fix: Index ui-ios public API (type names, doc comments, and the README sections) into agent-index.json and make `atom63 search`/`component` return them; add a coverage assertion to check:agent-index that every public Atom* type is indexed.

verified.reason: Reproduced. packages/ui-ios declares 101 unique public Atom* struct/enum/class/protocol names, and 68 of them never appear in packages/cli/generated/agent-index.json. The only Atom names in the index are about 30 component types, such as AtomButton, AtomMessage and AtomTokens. AtomAppBar and AtomDensity are absent, and `atom63 search AtomAppBar` and `atom63 search ios` both return 'No results'. build-index.mjs reads ui-ios only for Swift token names. The CLI README claims iOS coverage ('the shared web and iOS contract'). case-studies-round-13a.md confirms iOS builders read the README and the MCP and missed AppBar and compact density, though it blames the README framing more than the missing index entries. The gap in iOS findability is real.

findings.subject: apps/docs (docs coverage and Markdown twins)
findings.summary: Whole published entry points have no docs page and no CLI index entry: @atom63/ui-react/media, /media/lightbox, /theme controls, much of /layout, @atom63/mdx and @atom63/brand.
findings.evidence: Against packages/ui-react/api/*.api.md, values found nowhere in agent-index.json: media-lightbox 28/28, media 13/14 (VideoDialog, MediaLightbox, VideoThumbnail), theme 21/26 (AppearanceSection, SwatchTokenControl), layout 16/21 (ReaderLayout, PageSkeleton, GridChrome). Index string counts: '@atom63/mdx' 0, '@atom63/brand' 0. `atom63 search lightbox|ReaderLayout|PageSkeleton|logo` -> 'No results'. apps/docs/vite-plugins/llms-txt.ts:163 reads only index.ts, calendar and layout and claims that covers 'every component family'. check:agent-index only checks staleness (packages/cli/scripts/build-index.mjs:245-253).
findings.fix: Add docs pages (or catalog entries) for the media, lightbox, theme-controls and remaining layout exports and for @atom63/mdx and @atom63/brand; extend the index to them; add a check that every value in the published API reports is reachable from the index or explicitly marked internal.

verified.reason: Mostly reproduced. VideoDialog, MediaLightbox, VideoThumbnail, SwatchTokenControl, ReaderLayout, PageSkeleton and GridChrome each occur 0 times in agent-index.json, and AppearanceSection occurs once. The index has no '@atom63/mdx' string, and packages/mdx is a public versioned package. ui-react's package.json exports ./media and ./media/lightbox. llms-txt.ts:163 reads only index.ts, calendar/index.ts and layout/index.ts, yet its comment claims 'every component family'. The stale-index check in build-index.mjs only compares the generated file against the committed one. Two corrections: @atom63/brand is `private: true`, so it is not a published entry point and that part is wrong. ReaderLayout does appear once in pattern-layout.mdx:51, so 'no docs page' overstates that case. The media, lightbox and theme entry points are still undiscoverable to agents, so P1 stands.

findings.subject: all-contracts
findings.summary: State names drift across contracts in ways the consistency lint does not catch: focus vs focus-visible, rest vs default vs idle, hover vs hovering, pressed vs active.
findings.evidence: `focus` is the listed state in input.json:11, textarea.json:7, breadcrumb.json:7, item.json:25, search-field.json:6, toggle-group.json:10 and toggle.json:8 while 21 contracts use `focus-visible` and AGENTS.md rule 11 forbids :focus rings (input only papers over it with stateAliases focus->focus-visible, input.json:155; textarea/search-field crossRenderer.requiredStates also say `focus`, textarea.json:48, search-field.json:38). Resting state is `rest` in 29 contracts but `default` in field.json:8, form.json:7, frame.json:22 and `idle` in feedback-state.json:17, load-more-trigger.json:7, resizable.json:8, scroll-area.json:8, scrollable-list.json:8. scroll-area uses `hovering` (19 others `hover`). `active` means current/selected in input-otp, navigation-menu, sidebar-nav-tree while button/toggle use `pressed`. `node scripts/design-system/check-contract-consistency.mjs` -> "Contract consistency OK (76 contracts)" with none of these in contract-consistency-baseline.json.
findings.fix: Add these synonyms to lib/contract-consistency.mjs (focus->focus-visible where the recipe draws :focus-visible, default/idle->rest, hovering->hover), baseline them, then rename in contracts with stateAliases for one release.

verified.reason: Reproduced from source. input/textarea/breadcrumb/item/search-field/toggle-group/toggle list `focus` while about 21 contracts use `focus-visible`, and accordion/button use `focusVisible`. Resting state is `default` in field/form/frame and `idle` in resizable/scroll-area/scrollable-list/feedback-state, against `rest` elsewhere and `resting` in badge. scroll-area uses `hovering`. input-otp and navigation-menu use `active`. `node scripts/design-system/check-contract-consistency.mjs` prints "Contract consistency OK (76 contracts)." Only input has a stateAliases entry. Mitigation: `focus` on text fields behaves like :focus-visible. Even so, this is exactly the C2 near-synonym class the lint misses.

findings.subject: all-contracts
findings.summary: Of the 31 cross-renderer contracts only Button and Badge map their axes to iOS; the other 29 map states only, and conformance tests check states and outcomes, never axes.
findings.evidence: Only button.json and badge.json carry intent.platforms.ios axis maps; input.json maps only size md. dialog sizes, toggle sizes/tones, segmented-control sizes/variants/tones, slider/progress tones, tabs sizes, avatar sizes/shapes, card variants, item variants/sizes/tones, toaster tones, carousel dot axes have no iOS mapping. packages/ui-react/src/conformance/renderer-conformance.ts:3-9 records implementedStates and outcomes only. Where iOS axes are checked they are hard-coded literals, not read from the contract: packages/ui-ios/Tests/Atom63UITests/AtomVariantParityTests.swift:11-12 (`AtomFieldVariant == ["default","filled"]`, `AtomCardVariant == ["default","filled","elevated"]`).
findings.fix: Extend the `intent.platforms` map (props -> axes, with extensions) to every crossRenderer contract, generate the Swift enums from it as for Button/Badge, and make the generator fail when a web axis value is neither mapped nor an extension.

verified.reason: Reproduced. Only badge.json, button.json and input.json contain an `ios` platform block, and input's maps only minHitTarget. renderer-conformance.ts:3-9 records implementedStates and outcomes, with no axes. AtomVariantParityTests.swift:11-12 hard-codes `["default","filled"]` and `["default","filled","elevated"]` instead of reading the contract. iOS counterparts with axes exist (AtomCard, AtomAvatar, AtomToggle, AtomProgressView, AtomToast, AtomPageDots), and no documented decision defers their mapping.

findings.subject: progressive-blur
findings.summary: The CLI index publishes progressive-blur with `contract: null` and no check flags it.
findings.evidence: packages/cli/generated/agent-index.json component slug progressive-blur: contract null; check:agent-index passed (sweep/agent-index.log).
findings.fix: Covered by the bidirectional check in contracts-6; fix the instance with contracts-9.

verified.reason: Reproduced: agent-index publishes progressive-blur with contract null, and no check rejects it (it is the sole null). This is a C4 wiring gap. It largely overlaps contracts-9 but is a distinct check failure.

findings.subject: progressive-blur
findings.summary: progressive-blur is shown as Stable only because the catalog defaults missing maturity to stable.
findings.evidence: apps/docs/src/lib/component-catalog.ts:742 `getComponentMaturity(slug) ?? 'stable'`; CLI output "Status: Stable"; agent-index status stable with no contract.
findings.fix: Give it an explicit maturity in its new contract (preview until its layer-3 scorecard is ready) and remove the stable default (contracts-4).

verified.reason: Reproduced: component-catalog.ts:742 `getComponentMaturity(slug) ?? 'stable'`, and agent-index lists the status as stable. ui-react-stable-action-matrix.md:50 itself marks progressive-blur P0 "Do not promise stable compatibility until an owner... evidence are recorded", so Stable is dishonest.

findings.subject: badge
findings.summary: Badge `accent` and `neutral` mean different things on web and iOS inside the same contract.
findings.evidence: Web: badge.json:16 `accent` is a solid-variant extension "A neutral on the control hover surface" (intent.platforms.web extensions, ~:153); `neutral` is a palette hue (badge.json:43). iOS: intent.platforms.ios.props.tone.map (badge.json:241) maps `accent` -> tone primary, emphasis solid and `neutral` -> neutral soft; generated AtomBadgeTone (packages/ui-ios/Sources/Atom63UI/Generated/AtomComponentIntent.generated.swift:5-11) exposes `.accent`. A port of `<Badge variant="accent">` to `AtomBadge(tone: .accent)` changes neutral to brand solid.
findings.fix: Rename the iOS case to `primary` (deprecated alias `accent`) to match the intent tone axis, or rename the web extension; keep one meaning per name.

verified.reason: Reproduced. In badge.json, web `accent` is a variant extension described as "A neutral on the control hover surface" (around line 153), and `neutral` is a hue-group extension (line 224). The iOS tone map (around line 237) maps `accent` to primary/solid and `neutral` to neutral/soft. The generated AtomBadgeTone exposes `.accent`. Same name, different meaning within one contract: a C2 violation and a porting hazard.

findings.subject: amount
findings.summary: Amount has an iOS counterpart (AtomAmountText) that mirrors its `fractions` axis, but amount is not a cross-renderer contract and maps nothing.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-ios/Sources/Atom63UI/AtomAmountText.swift:6-12 ("Mirrors the amount contract's fractions axis"), Tests/Atom63UITests/AtomAmountTextTests.swift; amount.json has no crossRenderer; cross-renderer.json components list (31 entries) omits amount.
findings.fix: Add amount to cross-renderer.json with a crossRenderer block and an intent map for sizes and fractions; generate AtomAmountFraction from it.

verified.reason: Reproduced. AtomAmountText.swift:6-7 says "Mirrors the amount contract's `fractions` axis". amount.json has only $schema/component/contract/lists/maturity keys, with no crossRenderer or intent, and cross-renderer.json has 31 components and omits amount. Under C3 a web contract with an iOS counterpart must map its axes. Amount being preview does not remove the ready-blocking gap.

findings.subject: toggle
findings.summary: Toggle's pressed state is conveyed by background colour (neutral/accent) or by text colour alone (subtle), and the system has no forced-colors rules, so the state disappears in Windows High Contrast.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/toggle/toggle.css:137-153; grep -rn forced-colors packages/ui-react/src packages/styles/src returns only a comment at packages/ui-react/src/components/button/button.css:189; no @media (forced-colors) rule exists in the system.
findings.fix: Add @media (forced-colors: active) rules for [data-pressed] (e.g. background: Highlight; color: HighlightText, or a visible border/underline), and give tone=subtle a non-colour cue.

verified.reason: Pressed neutral and accent Toggles change only background-color and color, and subtle changes only color (toggle.css:137-153). A grep of packages and apps finds no @media (forced-colors) rule anywhere. The only hits are comments, changelogs, a CLI rule string and a figma test fixture. In forced colors, author backgrounds and colours are overridden, so pressed and unpressed look the same. aria-pressed still conveys the state to assistive tech, so this is a visual-mode gap (P1), not P0.

findings.subject: toggle-group
findings.summary: The selected segment loses all visual distinction in forced-colors mode, and toggle-group's roving keyboard focus is not covered by any APG binding or keyboard test.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/toggle-group/toggle-group.css:39-51 (fill and shadow only); apps/storybook/a11y/patterns.test.ts binds 9 components, none of them toggle-group; packages/ui-foundation/contracts/components/toggle-group.json has no accessibility block.
findings.fix: Add forced-colors rules for [data-pressed] segments and bind toggle-group to an APG pattern (toolbar-style roving tabindex) in the contract so patterns.test.ts plays arrow keys against its stories.

verified.reason: toggle-group.css:39-51 marks the selected cell with fill, gloss and shadow only, all of which forced colors drop. The system has no forced-colors rules. patterns.test.ts imports stories for accordion, alert-dialog, checkbox, dialog, dropdown-menu, radio, select, switch and tabs, but not toggle-group. toggle-group.test.tsx (109 lines) has no Arrow, keyboard or focus tests. The toggle-group contract has accessibilityOutcomes but no accessibility pattern binding.

findings.subject: panel-setting-button
findings.summary: An active PanelSettingButton differs from an inactive one only by background and border tint, so in forced-colors mode on and off tiles look identical.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/panel-setting-button/panel-setting-button.css:58-70; grep -rn forced-colors packages/ui-react/src packages/styles/src returns only a comment at packages/ui-react/src/components/button/button.css:189; no @media (forced-colors) rule exists in the system.
findings.fix: Add a forced-colors rule for [data-active] (Highlight border or background) or a non-colour on-state cue such as a check glyph.

verified.reason: panel-setting-button.css:58-70 makes [data-active] differ only by color-mix tints of action-primary on background, border and foreground. In forced colors, all three become system colours, and the border becomes the same colour as on an inactive tile. No forced-colors rule exists anywhere in the system, so on and off tiles look identical in High Contrast.

findings.subject: destination-link
findings.summary: DestinationLink ships no recipe: no class, no link colour or underline, no focus-visible style, no gap before the indicator and no Themes story, so it renders as plain body text in every theme.
findings.evidence: No CSS file in packages/ui-react/src/components/destination-link/; apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-destination-link-external-chromium-linux.png; destination-link.stories.tsx:38-39 'which has no Themes matrix'.
findings.fix: Add a .a63-DestinationLink recipe using --a63-text-link (or the link Button tokens), underline in prose, outline focus-visible, logical gap for the indicator, and a Themes story with baselines.

verified.reason: The destination-link directory holds only tsx, test, stories and index files, with no recipe CSS. The component sets no class on the anchor, only data attributes. The external snapshot shows 'View source' as plain body-coloured text with no underline, and the indicator butts against it with no gap. The stories file comments that the component 'has no Themes matrix'. The contract lists focus-visible as a required state, but the system defines no focus style for it (the only :focus-visible in styles/src is os/windows.css). The component doc calls it 'router-neutral link semantics', which partly explains the bare markup, but a stable contract with visualArchetypes 'action' and a required focus-visible state still ships no visual treatment. P1 stands.

findings.subject: radio
findings.summary: In forced-colors mode a checked radio looks the same as an unchecked one.
findings.evidence: radio.css:78-84 (dot is a ::before with background-color) and radio.css:91-94 (fill is background-color); no @media (forced-colors) rule in radio.css (grep across the batch: only button.css has one). Forced colors replace background-color with Canvas. Derived from CSS, not observed at runtime.
findings.fix: Add @media (forced-colors: active) { .a63-Radio-indicator::before { background-color: CanvasText; forced-color-adjust: none } .a63-Radio[data-checked] { border-color: Highlight } } (or draw the dot with a border), and capture a forced-colors story.

verified.reason: radio.css shows the checked state only through background-color (indicator fill, ::before dot at 78-84 and 91-94) and border-color. The repo has no forced-colors rule except in button.css. Base UI Radio is a span, not a native input. findings.subject: segmented-control

findings.subject: rating

findings.subject: search-field
findings.summary: SearchField drops a consumer ref and silently ignores size and invalid.

findings.fix: Merge the consumer ref with inputRef (callback ref), pass size and invalid to InputGroup instead of the inner input, and add tests for ref, size and invalid.

verified.reason: search-field.tsx spreads {...props} into InputGroupInput, then sets ref={inputRef} after it. On React 19 the consumer's ref is an ordinary prop, so it gets replaced. size and invalid also reach only the unstyled inner Input. InputGroup gets neither: it renders data-size from its own default (md) and no data-invalid. The sm/lg rules in input.css exclude [data-unstyled]. The invalid rule on the inner span only sets custom properties, but the group draws the border from its own properties. So the size and invalid chrome never change, which breaks the K1 rule that props match the contract and refs are forwarded.

findings.subject: field

With forced colors on, backgrounds become the system Canvas colour, shadows are dropped and outline stays none, so the focused row has no visible indicator. findings.subject: menu
findings.summary: Menu group labels fail text contrast: the recipe draws them in text-secondary at opacity 0.75 at the xs size, measured 3.36:1 on the modern light popup (WCAG 1.4.3 needs 4.5:1 for this size). Every Dropdown/Context/Menubar/Select label inherits it.

Measured on apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-menu-themes-chromium-linux.png: 'ACTIONS' label darkest pixel (138,138,138) on popup (252,252,252) = 3.36:1; same baseline aqua/dark label 3.19:1. verified.reason: Reproduced from the tokens, not only the screenshot. The label uses --a63-text-secondary, which resolves to surface-light-11 = rgba(100,100,100). With opacity 0.75 over a popup of about 252, that gives 0.75*100 + 0.25*252 = 138, i.e. (138,138,138). Contrast against 252 computes to 3.36:1. The label is 12-13px at weight 600, below the large-text size, so WCAG 1.4.3 asks for 4.5:1. Select, Command and Autocomplete labels reuse the same colour token. The opacity is set in menu.css, so it applies at least to the menu-based labels.

findings.subject: tabs
findings.summary: The selected tab in the default and underline variants is shown only by the indicator's background (a plate or a 2px bar) plus a text-color change, so in forced-colors mode the selected tab cannot be told from the others.

findings.subject: command

findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/command/command.test.tsx:54-90 ('renders the search input', 'renders the items from the items prop', 'replaces the input icon...'); no userEvent/fireEvent in the file; apps/storybook/a11y/patterns.test.ts:56-102 binds dialog, alert-dialog, dropdown-menu, tabs, select, switch, checkbox, accordion, radio only; packages/ui-foundation/src/a11y/index.ts:46-56 has no list-autocomplete combobox. verified.reason: command.test.tsx has exactly three tests (lines 54, 61, 68), all render-only, and none uses userEvent, fireEvent or the keyboard. findings.subject: scrollable-list
findings.summary: Activating a chevron scroll control can unmount the focused button, dropping keyboard focus to <body>; its labels are fixed English and the list has no accessible name.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/scrollable-list/scrollable-list.tsx:272-311 renders each control only while canScrollStart/canScrollEnd; :280,:301 aria-label literals; :18-41 no aria-label prop

verified.reason: I checked scrollable-list.tsx and the claim matches the code. A keyboard user who presses 'Scroll right' until the end therefore loses the focused element. The aria-labels 'Scroll left' and 'Scroll right' are literals that change only with RTL, and the props interface (lines 18-41) has no label or i18n prop and no ...rest, so adopters cannot localize them or name the list. The missing accessible name is the weakest part, because a plain div does not strictly need one. The focus loss and the fixed English labels alone are a real K2 focus-management and naming gap for a beta-supported component, so P1 stands.

findings.subject: sidebar

findings.fix: When data-state='collapsed' and collapsible='offcanvas', set inert on the container (or visibility:hidden after the transition) and add a test that collapsed links are not tabbable.

verified.reason: SidebarMenuButton (sidebar.tsx:564) and SidebarMenuSubButton (:752) set only data-active. findings.subject: marquee
findings.summary: In right-to-left layouts the marquee loop likely leaves a visible empty gap each cycle, because the keyframes always move left while duplicate tracks lay out to the left.

findings.subject: load-more-trigger
findings.summary: LoadMoreTrigger creates its live region in the same render that changes its text (and mounts a new one from hidden), so 'Loading more' and 'All items loaded' are often not announced, breaking the contract's announces-loading and announces-exhausted outcomes.

findings.fix: Render a persistent visually-hidden role=status region in every non-hidden state (including idle) and write the message into it on state change; keep it mounted across hidden by rendering the empty region; add a test that the same live-region node persists from idle to loading to exhausted.

verified.reason: The cited code is there. load-more-trigger.tsx:55-57 returns null while hidden. Lines 74-86 add role=status and aria-live only when the state is not idle, in the same render that swaps the message text. Going from idle to loading, the live-region attributes appear at the same moment as the new text, and many screen readers miss that change. Going from hidden to loading or exhausted mounts a fresh region with its content already inside, which is the well-known pattern that often goes unannounced. Also, with the hasMore/isLoading API alone the component goes hidden when hasMore is false, so the exhausted message renders only through an explicit state prop. The contract lists announces-loading and announces-exhausted as accessibility outcomes (load-more-trigger.json:47-52), and the test only checks the role after render. I did not test it with a screen reader. The pattern is a known failure and it blocks the contract's own accessibility outcomes, so P1 holds.

verified.reason: Partly true. dialog/select/tooltip contracts do say maturity 'stable', and ui-react.api.md has 0 @beta/@alpha/@experimental tags. findings.subject: progress

findings.subject: progress

findings.subject: spinner

findings.subject: spinner

findings.fix: Default the svg to aria-hidden and let the caller own the status text, or render visually hidden text inside a status wrapper; document which.

findings.subject: spinner

findings.subject: field

findings.subject: input (AtomTextField), textarea (AtomTextEditor), field (AtomFormField)
findings.summary: iOS fields do not draw the disabled state, though conformance evidence claims it.

findings.subject: field (AtomFormField)

findings.fix: Apply .accessibilityLabel(title) (or accessibilityElement(children: .contain) with the title as label) to styledContent inside AtomFormField.

findings.subject: textarea (AtomTextEditor)

findings.fix: Decide whether the iOS counterpart of FormMessage is the error line inside AtomFormField (and AtomFormMessage maps to Alert/Notice instead), then record the mapping in a cross-renderer contract.

findings.subject: amount

findings.subject: Tailwind and shadcn bridges (tailwind/roles.json, theme.css, compat/shadcn.css)
findings.summary: The Tailwind bridge exposes no text role for danger, accent or tertiary text, so the natural utilities (text-primary, text-destructive) paint fills as text and fail contrast.
findings.evidence: roles.json has no --a63-text-danger/-accent/-tertiary mapping; craft-rules.mjs:36-46 documents text-primary at 2.9:1 on the dark page; craft-baseline.json token-role entries in templates getting-started-checklist.tsx (text-primary) and mdx-live-preview.tsx (text-destructive); theme.css:88-97 exposes raw --color-danger-* steps.
findings.fix: Add roles such as text-danger, text-accent (brand text) and text-tertiary to roles.json and regenerate; point the role rule's message at them; stop re-exposing the raw status ramps (--color-danger-*, --color-info-*, ...) to Tailwind or mark them reference-only.

verified.reason: The gap itself is real. roles.json maps destructive to --a63-action-danger, foreground to text-primary and accent to the neutral hover plate, and it has no role for --a63-text-danger, --a63-text-accent or --a63-text-tertiary. theme.css exposes raw --color-danger-* steps. craft-baseline.json has the two cited entries (mdx-live-preview.tsx text-destructive, getting-started-checklist.tsx text-primary). It is mitigated, though. The craft-rules token-role check flags exactly this misuse in TSX and points to the text roles through the arbitrary form text-(--a63-text-danger), so new cases are caught and the existing ones are tracked baseline debt. This is an ergonomics gap rather than one that blocks 'ready'.

findings.evidence: app-shell.tsx:112-115; templates-pages-dashboard-page-phone-chromium-linux.png shows an empty bar with one icon.
findings.fix: Show the product name (or current page title) in the top bar below md. Provisional: composition, YZ confirms.

findings.subject: Page
findings.summary: Page has a boolean noPadding in place of a padding axis and no story or baseline.
findings.evidence: page.tsx:6 'noPadding?: boolean'; only page.test.tsx exists, no Page story.
findings.fix: Add a story; consider padding: 'default' | 'none' to match Container's padding axis.

findings.subject: app-view (page template)
findings.summary: The `atom63 build` phone snippet hands builders the same env() top padding that bypasses --a63-safe-area-top.
findings.evidence: `pnpm -s atom63 build "phone music player app"` snippet: '<div className="flex flex-col gap-4 pt-[env(safe-area-inset-top)]">'.
findings.fix: Change the snippet with layout-4.

findings.subject: ReaderLayout
findings.summary: Widths are raw Tailwind sizes rather than the Container max-width scale the other layout primitives share.
findings.evidence: reader-layout.tsx:23 'max-w-5xl', :25 'xl:max-w-4xl', :35 'w-64'; container.tsx uses containerFrameClassName(maxWidth).
findings.fix: Express the frame and measure through max-width.ts presets.

findings.subject: auth-card, empty-state, page-header, settings-section, data-table-section, settings-page, sign-in-page, ReaderLayout
findings.summary: No template story exercises long, CJK or unbroken strings, so wrap and truncation behaviour is judged from code only.
findings.evidence: None of the template stories under packages/templates/src/**/*.stories.tsx defines long-copy args (grep of exports: Desktop, Phone, Themes plus state stories).
findings.fix: Add a shared LongContent args set to story-matrix.tsx and a LongContent story per template.

findings.subject: Theme: retro
findings.summary: Figma shows the default for retro-dark field background and widget rim border colors.
findings.evidence: atom63.figma-sync.json skipped: --a63-field-background, --a63-widget-rim-border-color, --a63-segment-track-background.
findings.fix: Represent the 4-side rim as four color variables; sync the field background hook.

findings.subject: Brand ramps (b1-b6, auto) and brand action
findings.summary: Auto brand contrast is guaranteed by construction, not by a test across hues.
findings.evidence: auto-primary.ts RAMP_STEPS; personalization-axes.browser.test.ts:177-193 tests one value.
findings.fix: Add a test that generates ramps for a hue sweep and checks the brand pairs.

findings.subject: Brand ramps (b1-b6, auto) and brand action
findings.summary: Brand b6 is red, so a b6 primary action reads as destructive.
findings.evidence: brand-action.css b6 block; danger-600 rgb(187,29,34).
findings.fix: Decide whether b6 stays red.

findings.subject: Surface palettes (n1-n6) and surface tint
findings.summary: --a63-media-surface is restated identically in each surface block.
findings.evidence: surface.css:37,65,93 and the n4-n6 blocks.
findings.fix: Declare it once on :root, [data-a63-surface].

findings.subject: Space scale and density
findings.summary: Density 'comfortable' equals the default, so the axis has one effective alternative.
findings.evidence: environment.css:89-91; token-economy.log restate notice.
findings.fix: Document comfortable as the explicit default or add a spacious step.

findings.subject: Radius scale and radius axis
findings.summary: Radius steps change increment at the anchor (0.2 below, 0.4 above) without a note.
findings.evidence: foundation/radius.css multipliers.
findings.fix: Document the two increments in the scale comment.

findings.subject: Motion durations and easings
findings.summary: Reduced motion zeroes only four duration tokens; normal and slow are left to each component.
findings.evidence: motion.css:22-29; navigation-menu.css uses --duration-normal 11 times.
findings.fix: Zero --a63-motion-* durations as a set, or document that recipes own reduced motion.

findings.subject: Motion durations and easings
findings.summary: Swift Motion reads primitives, not semantic names, and nothing checks motion parity.
findings.evidence: generate-swift-tokens.mjs:437-440.
findings.fix: Generate from --duration-fast/--duration-normal and add motion/space/radius to swift-parity.
